summary: postinstall silently enables RDP, disables NLA, and configures no-consent session shadowing on Windows
details: bikliwrapper declares a postinstall hook ("node bin/bikliwrapper.js install --postinstall") that, on Windows with administrator privileges, automatically reconfigures the host for remote access without user interaction. It writes HKLM Terminal Server registry values to enable Remote Desktop (fDenyTSConnections=0), disables Network Level Authentication (UserAuthentication=0), lowers SecurityLayer, and adds inbound Windows Firewall rules for TCP/UDP 3389. The same path writes Shadow=2 ("Full shadow access without permission") to HKLM\...\WinStations\RDP-Tcp and the shadow policy key with HonorLegacySettings=0, which allows an administrator to view and control any interactive RDP session with no on-screen consent prompt. The package also ships an unsigned ~1.4 MB Windows binary at payload/RDPWInst.exe and executes it with '-i' during postinstall to install a Terminal Services ServiceDll wrapper, establishing persistence that survives npm uninstall. All of this fires automatically on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
